💬 Pakistan reaffirms Iran’s right to peaceful nuclear energy

📌 Islamabad, IRNA — Pakistan has reaffirmed that Iran, as a signatory to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT), has a legitimate right to develop and use nuclear energy for peaceful purposes.

Speaking at his weekly press briefing in Islamabad, Pakistani Foreign Ministry spokesperson Sajjad Haider said Pakistan’s position remained clear regarding Iran’s rights under the NPT.
​
His remarks came in response to questions about a resolution targeting Iran that was backed by the United States and three European countries (Britain, France and Germany) at the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA).
​
Haider said Pakistan considers Iran’s membership in the NPT an important basis for its right to pursue peaceful nuclear programs. He declined to provide further comments on the four countries’ action at the IAEA.
​
Moreover, the Pakistani spokesperson rejected a Reuters report alleging that Islamabad had sent a message to Tehran concerning developments in Yemen, saying the report was not accurate.
​
Addressing regional security, Haider said a joint defense pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey is defensive in nature and that there is currently no decision to admit another member.
​
He added that Pakistan supports stability and security in Yemen, backs international initiatives aimed at resolving the crisis, and supports Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. Pakistan, he said, will continue supporting efforts to promote peace and stability in Yemen and across the region.
